newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African Moslems placed under house arrest.
newsitem.headline: S.African Moslems placed under house arrest.

text.p: Twenty-five South African Moslem activists on Friday were placed under house arrest pending trial in February on charges including attempted murder following an anti-drugs protest that turned violent.

Most of the men, all members of People Against Gangsterism and Drugs (Pagad), were arrested on Monday when they staged an illegal protest outside Cape Town's airport, demanding tougher police action against drug-dealing gangs.
Eight more were arrested that night when masked Pagad members attacked a police station, seriously wounding two policemen and lightly wounding three more.
Pagad commander in chief Aslam Toefy joined them on Thursday when he surrendered to police two hours after a deadline set by the province's chief prosecutor, Attorney General Frank Kahn.
"All the accused are under permanent house arrest and only those who are working can leave their homes between 6 am and 7 pm," prosecutor Kevin Rossouw said during a bail application on Friday.
"All the accused will not participate in any marches of any kind until the case has been finalised," he said in a report on negotiations that had lasted almost five hours.
Pagad gained prominence in August when supporters publicly killed drug-baron Rashaad Staggie. Since then, the group has increasingly come into conflict with police over their war against gangsterism.
Describing Pagad as "just another gang", police accuse the movement of fire-bomb and grenade attacks on the homes of alleged drug members.

About 200 Pagad supporters waited outside the court, which was cordoned off with razor wire. As the accused emerged onto the street, their supporters chanted Allahu Akbar (God is Great). Only family members were allowed inside court.
